turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the computer's crawling. Bear with me a tick. You're Mark Ellison?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Who's come with you? I had the wrong file open.
[SEG0004] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Jess, his partner. I booked it. He's home with me all day, and he kept telling me he was fine.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): What's the worry?
[SEG0006] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Since the warehouse made him redundant he's been sleeping badly, no energy, and he's lost interest in everything.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): When was that redundancy? The screen just blinked, say it again.
[SEG0008] person_3 (CAREGIVER): End of July. About four months ago.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mark, how are you in yourself?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm fine.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sleeping through?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the keyboard got that. You're not sleeping?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0015] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He's in bed around eleven and awake at three, five or six nights a week, for the whole four months. Just lies there.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mark, awake at three most nights?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): And your energy?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Low.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Low. Low energy? A popup covered your answer.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0022] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He walked the dog before every shift. Now he's on the couch till the arvo. Knackered, and he still won't nap.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy? Footy, your mates?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0025] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He hasn't put a game on since August, hasn't rung his brother either.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): How's your mood? Down at all?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Down.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Since when? I didn't catch the start.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Down since the job.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Appetite changed?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Eating as usual, then?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): What are you doing with your days?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Nothing. Say a bit more, I was typing.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Don't care. Footy neither.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): I have to ask this gently. Any thoughts about hurting yourself, or not wanting to wake up?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not even a passing thought?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0042] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He's grumpy and withdrawn, not that. I would have told you.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Are you on any tablets, from us or the chemist?
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0045] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He tried Restavit a few weeks back, two nights. Woke up foggy, so he stopped.
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you remember the dose? I didn't see a number.
[SEG0047] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Just whatever the packet said. No idea of the milligrams.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Were there any blood tests for this tiredness? I've got nothing on the screen.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Borderline.
[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): Borderline what? Repeat that, a reminder popped up.
[SEG0051] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Thyroid test, the GP near the servo, about a year ago. They said it was borderline and he should repeat it. He didn't.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): I won't start a medicine today. Sertraline can lift this sort of flat mood, but we'll only look at it next time if you're still down after the bloods.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay.

[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll order a repeat thyroid test and a full blood count. Same time out of bed each morning if you can, and leave the phone out of the bedroom. Come back in a fortnight. If any thought of harming yourself turns up, don't sit on it, come in or ring the same day.

[SEG0056] person_1 (DOCTOR): Working impression, a depressive dip after the redundancy. Not confirmed, the bloods might still change it. You look tired, and your speech is slower than I'd expect, though you're following me alright.
[SEG0057] person_3 (CAREGIVER): We'll sort the form at the desk. He wanted Maccas on the way home, which is the most he's wanted anything all week.

Negative finding not recorded: patient denied taking any tablets from the clinic or over the counter at present.
Restavit dose was unknown; caregiver said it was 'whatever the packet said' and did not know the milligrams.
Prior thyroid test context not recorded: it was done about a year ago by another GP ('the GP near the servo'), was said to be borderline, and he was advised to repeat it but did not.
Negative finding not recorded separately: patient said he still won't nap despite being tired.
Symptom/history detail not recorded: patient described his days as 'Nothing' and 'Don't care,' consistent with marked inactivity/amotivation.
Safety advice detail omitted: if any thought of harming himself turns up, he should not sit on it and should come in or ring the same day.
